warning_texts: analysis/answers/R02.json misstates the dedup rule (first revision kept, attributed to the spec) while every figure was computed with the latest revision; if the caveat reaches the release it tells readers the wrong method and puts false words in the spec's mouth.

Answer caveat text in analysis/answers/ is checked by no deterministic rule in audit/check_plan.json (questions_are_answered only requires the question and facts fields), so a misstated method in an answer passes the machine gate silently.

Both test p-values are stored as 0.0000000000 with display_digits 4, and the statistics carry six decimals with display_digits 2; the true p-values are about 3e-157 (completion) and below double precision (AOV), so a release should show them as below 0.0001 rather than as exactly zero, and the store

audit/results/worker_analysis/result.json carries a placeholder summary, a created_at of 2026-01-01 and a single self-check value (0.473684) that matches none of this dataset's claims, so the worker's own result gives no evidence of the work it describes.

recompute_estimate, recompute_test and min_group_size in gate_claims_machine read clean_data/orders_clean.csv rather than raw; my raw-rooted recalculation agrees with them, but only claims_recomputed goes back to the export.
